You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: Calling Flush on the ETag response writer sends buffered bytes to the client before the response is complete, so the ETag can no longer be set (the request says Flush must not bypass the buffer).

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Trailers are lost. `finish` does `clear(h)` and then `maps.Copy(h, ew.snapshot)`, so header values set after the body is written (which net/http sends as trailers when the key is declared in `Trailer`) are discarded. Criterion 11 requires late changes to behave "same as without the middleware", and without it the trailer arrives. Reproduced: `without ETag trailer="abc123", with ETag trailer=""` (probe: handler sets `Trailer: X-Checksum`, writes "hello", then sets `X-Checksum`; client read over httptest.Server). Fix idea: snapshot the trailer keys at finish or copy the trailer map through, or only drop non-trailer changes.
- [minor] `FEATURE_FLOW.md` is untracked in the repo root and is not part of the stated change. Not mine; the orchestrator should confirm it is intended.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
Repo /tmp/ff-eval-w7391v_j/workspace. Fix round for the new middleware/etag.go (tests in middleware/etag_test.go). Reviewer reproduced one blocking bug:

- Trailers are lost on a buffered 200. `finish` does `clear(h)` then `maps.Copy(h, ew.snapshot)`, which discards values the handler sets after writing the body. Without the middleware, net/http sends them as trailers when the key was declared in the `Trailer` header before WriteHeader, or when the key has the `http.TrailerPrefix` ("Trailer:") prefix. Repro: handler sets `w.Header().Set("Trailer", "X-Checksum")`, writes "hello", then sets `X-Checksum: abc123`; over httptest.Server the client's `resp.Trailer.Get("X-Checksum")` is "abc123" without ETag and "" with it.

Fix: when restoring the snapshot, carry over the current values of keys declared in the snapshot's `Trailer` header values (comma-separated, canonicalize with http.CanonicalHeaderKey) and of any key starting with http.TrailerPrefix; every other late change stays dropped (criterion 11 still holds, including a late ETag being ignored). Keep it small. Write the failing test first (httptest.NewServer, read resp.Body fully, then check resp.Trailer for both forms), then fix. Don't change other behavior or the doc comment except to mention nothing new.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
11. Header changes the handler makes after WriteHeader/first Write do not reach the client (same as without the middleware), including an ETag set late. Trailers (declared via `Trailer` or using `http.TrailerPrefix`) still reach the client, as without the middleware.
(All other criteria unchanged; the existing tests encode them.)

CHECKS: targeted `go test -race -run ETag ./middleware`; end: `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` (empty).
